transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Lena (Nimbus Eng Mgr), Marc (CTO), Priya (SRE), Avery (Dev)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood. quick intro, we'll run through the sdk quickstarts for python and typescript, auth options, and a few gotchas for env setup. conner's gonna demo the repo.
[00:18] Marc: sounds good, quick note we care about latency on the checkout flow, and also PII, so encryption and retention are big.
[00:26] Connor: cool yea we'll hit KMS and retention — just FYI some of the auto-transcripts say K-V cash sometimes so apologies for that, it's KV cache.
[00:35] Lena: also interested in the console side, like how to view token usage per route.
[00:41] Connor: console.redwood.ai has per-route dashboards; we'll point to the quickstart and the SDK repo on GitHub.
[00:47] [01:00] Connor: i'll share my screen, starting in the python quickstart. first step, pip install redwood-inference (note: package name in pip may differ in preview docs). set REDWOOD_API_KEY as env var, or use SSO if you want org-level auth. here's a sample snippet:
[01:22] Connor: from redwood import Client
            client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
            response = client.generate("checkout upsell prompt")
This is pseudo, but the flow is simple: auth, create client, call.
[01:45] Lena: do you have support for oauth flows or more ephemeral creds for frontend?
[01:51] Maya: we recommend server-side calls for generation, and short-lived tokens for client access via our session tokens feature (we can share patterns).
[02:05] Marc: what about typescript? we'd prefer a typed SDK for node.
[02:10] Connor: we have an official typescript SDK; npm install @redwood/inference. example:
[02:18] Connor: import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'
            const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
            const res = await client.chat.create({ messages })

[02:35] Priya: in terms of env setup, any gotchas on docker images or proxies? we're behind corp proxy and use internal registries.
[02:43] Connor: good question — for corp proxies, ensure outbound to api.redwood.ai is allowed, and set standard http_proxy env vars. for docker, include api key via build-time ARG or mount at runtime; avoid baking secrets into images.
[03:05] Avery: we use terraform for infra — any IaC modules?
[03:09] Maya: we have example terraform snippets for dedicated and for VPC peering in the private docs; i'll attach links.
[03:18] [10:12] Connor: diving into auth: two common patterns — API keys per service and SSO/SAML for enterprise. For hosteds customers, API keys encrypted at rest; for private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. retention policies can be configured per account or per-route.
[10:35] Marc: can you guarantee deletion for logs? compliance team will ask for audit trails.
[10:41] Maya: we support configurable retention and can provide audit logs; we also have SOC 2 and ISO attestations (we'll share the pack).
[11:00] Lena: on the SDK side, how do we do batching for throughput?
[11:06] Connor: SDK supports batch endpoints and you can set max_batch or streaming.concurrency in client config. default batching is automatic if you use the batch API; for low-latency checkout calls we recommend small batches and pin to a latency-optimized model variant.
[11:34] Lena: model variants — are those auto-fallbacks?
[11:38] Connor: yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible quantized variant if the primary is unavailable; you can pin versions in the request or at the route level.
[12:02] [18:00] Maya: quick demo switch — Connor will run the TypeScript quickstart live from the repo.
[18:12] Connor: cloning repo, open examples/ts/checkout-demo. npm i, set env, then node run. here's the sample payload we use for the 'upsell' model — it's deliberately tiny to keep latency low.
[18:35] Connor: small typo in docs: 'max_tokens' default is 512 but our snippet says 1024 in one place — we'll fix that.
[18:42] Avery: good catch.
[19:05] Connor: running the call now — response comes back in ~120ms in my local run against hosted dev region, your mileage will vary.
[19:17] Marc: that's promising. what about dedicated vs hosted pricing for sustained traffic?
[19:24] Maya: for sustained high QPS, Dedicated capacity is more predictable and cheaper per-token; Hosted is simpler to start. we'll send a cost comparison for your expected checkout rates.
[19:41] Priya: and encryption keys? we want to use our KMS.
[19:44] Connor: Private deployment and Dedicated both support customer-managed KMS; hosted can integrate with customer KMS for enterprise tiers. we'll include the KMS integration doc.
[20:05] [27:30] Lena: any known pitfalls integrating with our node service that uses serverless functions? cold start is a concern.
[27:38] Connor: for serverless, avoid instantiating client on every invocation; reuse across warm invocations, and consider async job for heavy embeddings. Also use caching and prefix KV cache for repeated prompts.
[27:58] Marc: KV cache sounds new to some of our infra folks — any specifics?
[28:05] Connor: KV cache caches prefix key-values for decoder states to speed autoregressive calls, reduces tokens and latency — some docs mistakenly call it K-V cash in transcripts so ignore that.
[28:28] Maya: we'll share a short note and an example of reusing clients in AWS lambda.
[28:32] Priya: do you have examples for streaming responses to the browser?
[28:37] Connor: yes, the TS SDK supports server-sent events and websockets patterns; we'll share the snippet.
[29:00] [35:00] Maya: recap — action items: we'll send quickstart links, sample payloads, benchmark checklist, and security pack. Nimbus will run a 1-day smoke test and confirm SSO/KMS details. after that we can scope a poc.
[35:20] Marc: ok good, please include estimated cost for a 1-week poc and for 3-month dedicated commit.
[35:28] Maya: will do.
[35:35] Lena: thanks all, this was helpful.
[35:40] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with links. end.
